summary: Internal working copy of an assay-control training deck on plate acceptance, with the legacy Osterquill cover. The body explains how control validity is judged for in vitro plates and how a failed plate is handled. It is not a client deliverable and it is superseded by the approved training version.

slides.title: Plate acceptance and control validity
slides.subtitle: In vitro assay-control training | Working copy 09/24/2024

slides.title: Purpose of this session
bullets: Who signs off a plate before its data are used
What makes a control valid for each in vitro package
What to do when a plate fails, and who has to be told
slides.notes: NK: Lucia asked for the failed-plate route to be first, not last. Move it before the walk-through if there is time.

slides.title: Control validity: the basics
bullets: Every plate carries its own positive and negative controls
Control validity is judged against the criteria in the study plan, not on the day

bullets.text: Criteria are fixed before the first plate is read

bullets: A plate with an invalid control is not used for a potency or safety call

bullets.text: Vehicle and cell-free wells on every plate
Strain-specific positive controls with and without S9

bullets_right.text: Vehicle and reference clastogen per culture

slides.title: Plate acceptance on the day
bullets: Check the vehicle wells against the range in the study plan before reading the test wells
Check the reference compound response against its own range
Record the plate ID and the reader settings on the observation sheet

bullets.text: Initials and date on every printed plate map

slides.notes: KM: The vehicle range wording is from the old SOP. Confirm with Lucia before this version is reused.

boxes: Control outside range > Stop the read
Repeat plate or exclude > Amendment if needed

slides.title: What goes in the study record
bullets: Plate acceptance decision and who made it
Any repeat plate, with the reason
Study amendment reference if the criteria changed during the work
